title: Strike off a fresh fill to its screed rails, keeping the drain box-out empty and wasting no fill
instruction: Strike off the fresh fill to the screed rails. Drag the grey screed board along both rails, both ends on the rails, so that no ball stands above the rail tops and the low spots in the surface are filled, and push what is left off the far end into the waste trough. The box-out in the middle of the form is a drain opening and must stay empty. There is only a little more fill than the low spots need, so do not waste it. You may use the two hand floats. Leave no ball anywhere else on the table.
context: Concrete crews strike off fresh concrete with a straightedge screed riding on two screed rails set to the finished level (ACI 302.1R): high material is carried ahead in a roll to fill low spots, and the surplus is pushed off the end. Box-outs for drains and sleeves must be kept free of concrete, so material in line with one is moved aside by hand float before the screed passes. Ready-mix is ordered with only a small overage, so a crew that wastes the roll ahead of the screed is left with low spots.
setup: A wooden table; positions are from the midpoint between the two arm bases, measured forward and toward the left arm. Two fixed steel screed rails (190 x 6 x 30 mm tall) run forward from 195 to 385 mm, centred 78 mm left and right of the midline. Between them, from 220 to 340 mm forward, is a fixed grey base slab 17 mm thick, closed by a fixed wooden stop board at 217 mm (6 mm thick, 30 mm tall) and an end board at 343 mm (6 mm thick, 26 mm tall). The fill is a grid of 10 x 12 cells, 12 mm apart, of 12 mm plastic balls (4 g) on the slab. A fixed red box-out (21 x 21 mm inside, 1.5 mm walls, flush with the rail tops) stands on the midline at 292 mm in place of four cells. 104 grey balls fill the other cells except six low spots, each two cells missing side by side across the groove between two rows: three on each side of the form, at 262, 274 and 298 mm forward, none in line with the box-out. 12 tan balls of the same kind rest in the pockets of the fill over its two near columns, at least 20 mm in from the rails: four on each side and four in line with the box-out; each sits in the groove that leads to one low spot, or one groove inside it. Past the end board is a waste trough to 392 mm, 164 mm wide, with 30 mm wooden walls. A grey screed board (14 x 200 x 25 mm, 80 g) rests across both rails at 205 mm, behind the stop board. Two blue hand floats (50 x 6 x 25 mm, 20 g) lie on the table at 150 mm forward, 135 mm left and right.
scoring: A ball stands high if it is in the form and its top is more than 1 mm above the rail tops; it is in the box-out if its centre is inside the box-out's walls; a low spot is filled when a ball rests on the base slab inside it. 0.3 once no ball stands high, the box-out is empty and at least 94 balls rest on the base slab; +0.5 if at least five of the six low spots are filled; +0.2 if every ball is in the form or the waste trough, none elsewhere. Doing nothing scores 0 (the surplus stands above the rails); pushing the surplus straight down the form drops some into the box-out (0); pushing it all into the trough leaves the low spots empty (0.5). Success once the score is 1.0 and the balls are still for 1 s.
reset_notes: Put the grey balls back in their cells (leaving the six low spots), the tan balls in their 12 pockets over the two near columns, the screed across the rails behind the stop board, and the hand floats on their marks beside the rails.
fidelity: Fresh concrete is modelled as one layer of loose 12 mm balls on a set base with surplus balls on top, so it rolls and drops into low spots when pushed but does not slump or bleed. The screed and hand floats are rigid boards; the rails, forms and box-out are fixed.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0 (step limit reached, task not completed); demo: 1.0
